rows.desc_en: Built under the Earth Fed. Forces' Operation V. Later given magnetic coating.
The Federation's first mass-produced mobile suit. Uses combat data from Amuro's Gundam.
The Red Comet Char Aznable's own Zaku. Its thrust is up by about 30%.
Large Newtype MS. Highly mobile, with mega particle cannons all over its body.
Giant MA Lt. Gen. Dozle flew at Solomon. Its short operating time is its weakness.
Built under the Fed. Forces' Operation V. Artillery MS made for mid-range support.
Zeon's main general-purpose MS, the most produced unit of the One Year War.
Heavy MS for ground combat. Known for fast hover movement and its Giant Bazooka.
A Dom modified for space. Deployed in large numbers, replacing the Zaku II F Type.
Zeon's last high-end production MS. A lack of pilots kept it from showing its worth.
Field-modified custom of a Gundam Ground Type wrecked fighting the Apsaras.
Ground unit built from surplus RX-78 parts. About 20 were made and sent to Asia.
Custom redesign fixing the Gouf's flaws: narrow attack range and low versatility.
Zeon prototype MA. Has a huge mega particle cannon and the ability to fly.
A Zaku II F Type with its space equipment removed, modified for ground use.
Official name: Gundam NT-1. An experimental Newtype unit incorporating new technology.
Lightly armored, highly mobile assault MS. Carries many solid-ammo weapons.
Integrated Re-engineering Program Zaku II. Its mobility etc. exceed the Rick Dom's.
Space type of the Gundam Development Project's Unit 1. Has two big thrusters.
Unit 2 of the Gundam Development Project. Designed for assaults with a tactical nuke.
Disguised form of the unit being built as Gundam Development Project Unit 4.
Unit 3 of the Gundam Development Project. A huge unit mainly for space base defense.
Large mobile armor built by Axis. Equipped with many beam cannons and an I-field.
An upgraded GM built after the One Year War. Issued to ace pilots.
The AEUG's transformable ace unit. Later enhanced with a bio-sensor.
The Zeta Gundam's high-speed mode. Can enter the atmosphere and fly solo in it.
A Titans-built Gundam Mk-II, stolen by the AEUG and repainted.
New-gen Gundam built by the Titans with new tech as a next mainstay MS candidate.
Upgrade of the GM, the Fed.'s One Year War mainstay. Its basic specs barely improved.
Units the AEUG seized from the Fed. Forces at its founding and used. Repainted green.
Capt. Quattro's gold-armored unit. It can't transform, but its basic specs are high.
Haman Karn's personal mobile suit. The first unit ever equipped with funnels.
Axis mass-production MS. Has simple transformation and a powerful beam cannon.
The Gaza C's MA mode. Mobility improves, but close combat becomes impossible.
Paptimus Scirocco's self-developed personal unit. Equipped with a bio-sensor.
Large transformable Newtype unit with psycommu. Boasts heavy firepower and armor.
The Psycho Gundam's mobile armor mode. It can fly using its Minovsky craft.
An Earth Fed. Forces unit for atmospheric use. Known for its unique disc shape.
With no melee weapons, the Asshimar's MA mode could well be called its true form.
Built mainly by ex-Zeon engineers. Lacking output, it's on par with the GM II.
To tell them from Titans units, the Earth Fed. Forces painted theirs blue.
rows.note: name follows glossary entry for the same unit

rows.desc_en: Adopted as a step up from the Hizack. Used mainly as a commander's unit.
The AEUG's top MS after the Zeta. Heavily armed and armored; transforms and combines.
Its versatility and stable performance befit the Zaku name, but cost was an issue.
Zaku III with swapped parts for commanders. Noted for extra weapons and propellant.
High-end production MS with heavy weapons incl. Incom. Flown by the Space Wolf team.
Giant Newtype mobile suit built with technology seized from the Titans.
Equal in performance to Haman's Qubeley. The dark blue one is Elpeo Ple's own.
rows.note: name built on glossary 'Qubeley Mk-2 (Ple-Two)' pattern

rows.desc_en: Equal in performance to Haman's Qubeley. This red one is Ple-Two's own.
Mass-produced Qubeley with the same specs, plus funnels and other added weapons.
A Zeta whose damaged head was swapped for a found Zaku II head. Not an official name.
Amuro's own unit, overwhelmingly strong, with a Psycho-Frame and fin funnels.
Char's crimson personal mobile suit. Powerfully armed, built around its funnels.
Meant as a simplified mass-production Zeta, but only prototyped. High basic specs.
The Back Weapon System is a detachable part that adds both flight ability and weapons.
The Fed.'s main mass-production MS after the GM III. So good it served 30 years.
Newtype unit armed with funnels. Piloted by Gyunei, a Cyber Newtype.
Of the two built, Quess used the red one. It has no commander's antenna.
Neo Zeon's main production MS. Developed by ex-Zeon engineers from the Zaku line.
A unit with commander customization. Dark blue is Ens. Rezin's personal color.
Large mobile armor for Newtypes. Has overwhelming firepower and an I-field.
Top unit of SNRI's small MS project. Armed with many new-generation beam weapons.
Crossbone Vanguard commander's mobile suit. Zabine Chareux's unit.
Crossbone Vanguard commander's mobile suit. Not the newest model, but high-spec.
A giant, oddly shaped mobile armor that Iron Mask (Carozzo) had secretly developed.
The Crossbone Vanguard's latest high-end MS. Piloted by Berah (Cecily).
Base unit of the Den'an line, Crossbone's main production MS. Mobile and versatile.
A Den'an-Zon of the "Black Vanguard" led by Zabine Chareux.
The VSBR-equipped version of the F90, base unit of SNRI's Formula Project.
Core unit of the new Crossbone Vanguard led by Berah. Excels at close combat.
Core unit of the new Crossbone Vanguard led by Berah. Piloted by Zabine Chareux.
Core unit of the new Crossbone Vanguard led by Berah. Piloted by Tobia Arronax.

rows.model_en: A boy living in Side 7. Caught in battle,
rows.desc_en: he becomes the Gundam's pilot. Awakening as a Newtype, he grows to be the strongest.

rows.model_en: White Base's Guncannon pilot. Once a cynic
rows.desc_en: and a coward, he finds meaning in the fight after meeting Miharu, a young girl spy.

rows.model_en: Amuro's classmate from Side 7. On White
rows.desc_en: Base, he mostly pilots the Guntank. Though small, he is fiercely competitive.

rows.model_en: Zeon's ace pilot, known as the Red Comet.
rows.desc_en: Behind his mask, he is really Casval, the orphaned son of Zeon Zum Deikun.

rows.model_en: Third Zabi son and born soldier, he led the
rows.desc_en: Space Attack Force and Solomon. He sortied in the Big Zam but fell to the Gundam.

rows.model_en: Rookie leader of the 08th MS Team, Kojima
rows.desc_en: Battalion. He bonded with Zeon's Aina Sakhalin, met in battle, and left the army.

rows.model_en: An MS pilot of the 08th MS Team and its
rows.desc_en: second-in-command. Sharp-tongued, she called her leader Shiro a softie at first.

rows.model_en: An MS pilot of the 08th MS Team. Two units
rows.desc_en: he served in were wiped out. It weighed on him, but Shiro helped him move past it.

rows.model_en: Daughter of the noble Sakhalin family and a
rows.desc_en: Zeon test pilot. Meeting enemy soldier Shiro Amada slowly changes how she lives.

rows.model_en: A veteran pilot serving the Sakhalins. In a
rows.desc_en: Gouf Custom, he let his revered Aina and the wounded escape, then fell, duty done.

rows.model_en: A Federation test pilot, known as Chris.
rows.desc_en: She grew fond of Bernie, met by chance, but unknowingly destroyed his Zaku.

rows.model_en: A Zeon recruit, known as Bernie. Young Al
rows.desc_en: learns who he is and joins him. He fights to save the colony, but meets a tragic end.

rows.model_en: A rookie test pilot at Torrington Base.
rows.desc_en: After the GP02 theft, he hurls himself into fierce battles with his nemesis Gato.

rows.model_en: An MS pilot instructor at Torrington, he
rows.desc_en: became the Albion's combat leader after the GP02 theft. He died in an MS accident.

rows.model_en: Zeon ace dubbed the Nightmare of Solomon.
rows.desc_en: Serving Delaz, he spearheaded Operation Stardust and waged a fierce fight with Kou.

rows.model_en: A Zeon officer. She joined the Delaz Fleet
rows.desc_en: intending all along to defect to the Fed. Gato and Kou foiled it; she died in battle.

rows.model_en: A civilian student who hated the Titans and
rows.desc_en: joined the AEUG. Hailed as Amuro reborn for his superb combat skill, he became an ace.

rows.model_en: The alias Char Aznable used after leaving
rows.desc_en: Axis, when he became an AEUG officer. He lost his fight with Haman and went missing.

rows.model_en: Once a Titans officer, she defected to the
rows.desc_en: AEUG after being shown their cruelty, and fought as one of its key pilots.

rows.model_en: Feared for his One Year War feats, he was
rows.desc_en: confined by the Fed. Roused by Katz, he joined Karaba, fighting with Hayato and co.

rows.model_en: A Titans pilot. Supposedly elite, he lost
rows.desc_en: again and again after meeting Kamille, and died without ever getting his revenge.

rows.model_en: A Titans Cyber Newtype pilot. She met
rows.desc_en: Kamille in Hong Kong. They fell in love, but Jerid shot her as she shielded him.

rows.model_en: A Newtype back from Jupiter. A charismatic
rows.desc_en: genius, he killed Jamitov and took over the Titans. Kamille's suicide charge slew him.

rows.model_en: Ex-Fed. major. Though he inwardly hated the
rows.desc_en: Titans, he did his duty well. Flying the Asshimar, he plagued the AEUG many times.

rows.model_en: A Titans ace pilot, belligerent enough to
rows.desc_en: be called a beast. A stubborn survivor, he later fought Judau and the others too.

rows.model_en: Guardian of Mineva, the last Zabi. She used
rows.desc_en: charisma and statecraft to unite Axis' Zeon remnants and return to the Earth Sphere.

rows.model_en: A Side 1 boy living tough as a junk dealer.
rows.desc_en: Scouted by the AEUG for his Newtype talent, he fights Haman in the ZZ.

rows.model_en: AEUG volunteer. On the Argama she mostly
rows.desc_en: flew the Zeta Gundam. After the war, she and Judau joined a Jupiter fleet's crew.

rows.model_en: After the Titans fell, she led Axis, now
rows.desc_en: Neo Zeon, nearly taking the Earth Sphere. Insisting on dueling Judau, she lost.

rows.model_en: A girl Glemy was training as a Newtype.
rows.desc_en: Drawn to Judau, she joined the AEUG. She died fighting her sister, Ple-Two.

rows.model_en: Said to be Ple's clone, or her sister. She
rows.desc_en: is combative. Fighting Judau, she hears the dead Ple's voice and turns on Glemy.

rows.model_en: Sworn to Haman, he prizes chivalry. After
rows.desc_en: repeated failures, Haman had him made a Cyber Newtype; he died a disposable pawn.

rows.model_en: Haman's fierce warrior. In new MS he often
rows.desc_en: plagued Judau's team, but ambition made him defect to Glemy. He fell to the ZZ.

rows.model_en: He rose from private to commander under
rows.desc_en: Haman, then suddenly rebelled from hidden ambition. Roux, whom he loved, killed him.

decisions: Desc fit checked with tools/textenc.wrap (380 px, 43 bytes/line): every desc_en wraps to 2 lines. The 43-byte line cap, not pixel width, is the binding limit, so real capacity is ~80-85 chars, not 85-90.

Pilot cards: model_jp is the first line of the bio and desc_jp continues it mid-sentence; model_en is written as the opening line (<=43 bytes) and desc_en continues the same sentence, cut at a matching English point.
Card names use the short card form (Full Burnern, Physalis, Dendrobium) rather than the glossary's long 'Gundam GPxx ...' unit names, matching the Japanese card names.
Abbreviations used: MS, MA, Fed., Lt. Gen., Capt., Ens., Ex-Fed., incl., co.
uncertain: U-18: 'Integrated Re-engineering Program' is marked unverified in the glossary; sentence restructured to fit ('Integrated Re-engineering Program Zaku II.').
U-48: 'Qubeley Mk-2 (Ple)' built on the glossary 'Qubeley Mk-2 (Ple-Two)' pattern; no glossary entry for the Ple version.
U-51: model ？？？ kept as '???'; name 'Z Zaku' is unverified in the glossary.
U-46: 'Space Wolf team' is unverified in the glossary.
P-06: 'Kojima Battalion' not in glossary; used the standard English name.
P-12/P-03: 'Al' and 'Guntank' not in glossary excerpt; used standard spellings.
